title: fix(cli)!: objectstack build --strict-body counts each callable once, and --json issues lists callables only
body:
Fixes #22839

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What was wrong (measured on `origin/main` `1eff3224d`)

`compile.ts`'s `--strict-body` block built `issues` as the body-extraction warnings plus one placeholder row whenever `count - bodyExtracted > 0`. The placeholder's origin was the word `aggregate` in angle brackets, and its reason was "N callable(s) lowered to handler ref but produced no body". The block then printed `issues.length` as the number of callables. At the door (`bin/run-dev.js build --strict-body`, the reverse leg below), one refused handler printed `--strict-body: 2 callable(s) lack a metadata body` and four printed `5`. `--json` `issues` carried the placeholder as an extra row beside the real ones.

## Premise check: are `missingBody` and the warnings the same callables? Not always

Measured with a tsx probe that runs `lowerCallables` and the old arithmetic over nine shapes:

| shape | old header | new header | new rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. CONTROL: 1 clean hook | 0 | 0 | none |
| B. 1 refused hook | 2 | 1 | `hook 'refused_1'` |
| C. 4 refused hooks | 5 | 4 | the 4 hooks |
| D. 1 `functions` map entry only | 1 (placeholder row only) | 1 | `function 'score_lead'` |
| E. 1 `functions` array entry + 1 refused hook | 2 | 2 | the hook, `function 'arr_fn'` |
| F. 1 hook with an authored `body` beside an inline `handler` | 1 (placeholder row only) | 1 | `hook 'clean_1'` |
| G. same refused hook at top level AND in `packages[0].manifest` | 3 | 1 | the hook, once |
| H. same clean hook at both levels + 1 `functions` entry | 0 (passed) | 1 | `function 'score_lead'` |
| I. same clean + refused hook at both levels | 2 | 1 | the refused hook, once |
| J. one handler shared by two clean hooks + 1 `functions` entry (one walk) | 0 (passed) | 1 | `function 'score_lead'` |

So the populations differ in three ways:

1. A `functions` entry has no `body` slot. It is never extracted, so it leaves no warning, and only the placeholder row counted it (D, E).
2. An inline function beside an authored `body` is never extracted either, so it also leaves no warning (F).
3. A stack carrying the same callable at the top level and inside a `packages[i].manifest` body is walked twice. `count` dedups by function identity, while extraction runs once per walk. Each refusal is recorded twice and each lowered body is counted twice (G, I). That hid the `functions` entry in H, so the old gate passed it.

## The fix

- `lowerCallables` (`packages/cli/src/utils/lower-callables.ts`) returns `bodylessCallables`. It holds one row per registered callable that no slot lowered into a body, each once, keyed by ref, in registration order. This is exactly the population the placeholder row counted, itemized. A refused handler's row is the extractor's refusal, unchanged (`origin`, `reason`, `kind`, `freeIdentifiers`). A `functions` entry, or an inline function beside an authored `body`, gets an `{ origin, reason }` row naming it (`function 'name'`, `hook 'name'`, `action 'name'`).
- `compile.ts`: `issues = lowering.bodylessCallables`. The header's wording is unchanged and its number is `issues.length`. The `--json` exit keeps the same `error` string and the same keys.
- **Landing point.** The claim's file surface named `compile.ts`, its tests and the changeset. The producer of the count is `lower-callables.ts` in the same package, so the fix lands there (producer side). `extract-hook-body.ts` is untouched.

**Why F stays a row.** Two definitions were possible. One is "a slot runs it from the runtime module", under which F is not a row, since the hook binder prefers `body`. The other is "no slot lowered it", under which F is a row. The second is the placeholder's own population, and F's function is still bundled (`needsBundle` reads `count - bodyExtracted`, which this PR does not touch). Under it, every stack in which each callable is bound at one slot gets exactly the verdict it got before. There `bodyExtracted` counts each lowered callable once, so `count - bodyExtracted` is this list's length, and the old gate refused iff that exceeded 0, which is iff this list is non-empty. The first definition would have let `--strict-body` pass F while the build still emitted `objectstack-runtime.*.mjs` beside it, so it would have widened the accept set. Verdicts move only from pass to refuse, and only where a callable lowered at two or more slots masked a callable that was never lowered. That is H, the same callable at the top level and in a package body, reachable only through the two-level hand-written shape. It is also J, one function bound as the handler of two or more hooks or actions in a single walk, beside a `functions` entry or an authored-`body` slot. Both are narrowings.

## Consumers of `--json` `issues` (measured, before the shape moved)

`git grep` over the tree at `1eff3224d` (`packages`, `scripts`, `.github`, `examples`, `packages/qa`, `content/docs`):

- The placeholder origin and its reason text: one hit, `compile.ts:340` (the producer). No reader.
- `strict-body: missing body`: `build-json-failure-warnings.e2e.test.ts:437`, which reads `error` and `warnings`, not `issues`. `truncation-remainder-notices.test.ts:411` is a source-text pin on the payload literal, unchanged here. `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json:1344` is a manual step that captures the payload and reads no row.
- `payload.issues` reads: `build-json-failure-warnings.e2e.test.ts:358` and `:394`, both on other exits (docs validation, capability preflight).
- No `--strict-body` invocation in `.github/workflows`, `scripts` or `examples`.

No reader of the placeholder row, so it is removed outright and no summary field is added.

## Docs

`content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx:173` ("`objectstack build --strict-body` fails on it") and `:345` ("turn extraction warnings into a hard build failure (exit 1) with a per-callable diagnostic") were re-read, and both are still true. No other `content/docs` page describes `--strict-body`'s output. No docs edit.

## Tests (all at `11d4d8c6e`, the head of this PR)

- `packages/cli/test/build-strict-body-count.test.ts` (new, `integration` project: it spawns the CLI) pins the triage's door pins. CONTROL with 0 refused: exit 0 and no header. 1 refused: the header reads 1 and lists 1 hook; `--json` `issues` has 1 entry. 4 refused: the header reads 4 and lists 4 hooks; `--json` `issues` has 4 entries, each `kind: 'free-identifiers'`. A `functions` entry beside a refused hook gives `issues` two origins: the hook, then `function 'sbc_score'`.
- `packages/cli/test/lower-callables.test.ts` (`unit`): 10 new cases over `bodylessCallables`. They cover the control, 1 and 4 refused, a refused action, `functions` entries (map, declared, array), an authored `body` beside an inline function (hook and action), a single walk whose list length equals `count - bodyExtracted`, a callable lowered at any slot, and the two double-walk cases. The divergence cases assert the old answer beside the new one.

```
vitest --project integration test/build-strict-body-count.test.ts   Tests 6 passed (6)          @ 11d4d8c6e
vitest --project unit (whole @objectstack/cli unit tier)             281 files, 4195 tests passed @ 11d4d8c6e
pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build && typecheck                    exit 0 (tsc --noEmit + check:test-typecheck; both new test files are in tsconfig.test.json's program, by --listFilesOnly)
```

The `integration` tier is otherwise declared to CI. Locally only the new integration file was run, because the diff adds it.

## Reverse verification (committed fix, ablation-replace WRAP mode, restore proven)

`compile.ts` loads from `src/` in the spawned child (`bin/run-dev.js` via tsx; `packages/cli/dist` was absent for the first leg A run and for legs B-prime and C; the final leg A re-run ran with dist built and still went red, so the child loads src — corrected by the seat from the dev's report), and the unit file imports `../src`. So no rebuild leg applies. Each mutation was proven on disk (anchor 1 to 0, blob changed), and each restore was proven (blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty).

- **Leg A** (`compile.ts` put back to warnings + placeholder) at `11d4d8c6e`: the integration file reds 5 of 6 with `Expected "1" Received "2"` and `Expected "4" Received "5"`, and the control stays green. Same result at `50fd36bbf`.
- **Leg B′** (`bodylessCallables` becomes the raw warnings): the unit file reds 5 of 19 (the `functions` entry, authored body, single-walk equality and both double-walk cases).
- **Leg C** (the lowered-at-any-slot filter dropped): the unit file reds 1 of 19.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` re-derived from this diff gives 65 families, the 54 named at dispatch plus 11 changeset-family gates the diff adds. All 65 were run, each exit code captured before any pipe, and `--ran` reconciles: 65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, all codes recorded. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage` first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: no `dist/` for packages outside the cli closure). After a full `turbo run build` they exit 0.

**Lint (proven narrowing, not `pnpm lint`).** First, ESLint's own API (`isPathIgnored` + `calculateConfigForFile`) says 4 of the 5 changed paths are linted; the changeset `.md` is not. Second, `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on those 4 files at `11d4d8c6e` lists 4 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. Third, invariance: `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting (its own comment says no `parserOptions.project` and no typed rules), has no cross-file import rules, and loads only two baseline JSONs that this diff does not touch. So this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Sibling defect, reported to the seat for filing (not fixed here).** `needsBundle` in `compile.ts` still reads `count - bodyExtracted`. On a stack carrying the same hook at the top level and in `packages[0].manifest` plus a `functions` entry, `objectstack build` (default) printed `Skipping legacy runtime bundle (all 2 callables are body-only)`, exited 0 and wrote no `objectstack-runtime.*.mjs`. The `functions` entry therefore ships with no implementation (measured on a scratch app). Fixing it changes which builds emit the bundle, so it is out of this card's scope.
- `composeStacks(…, { manifest: 'preserve' })` on main emits only `manifest` and `packages`; measured, its top-level keys are exactly those two. So the double walk is reachable only through a hand-written stack carrying both levels, the shape `build-multi-package-artifact.e2e.test.ts` builds. That file's comment says the shape is "the way `composeStacks` … writes it", which no longer holds.
- Triage's grade wrote `Clause-②: yes`, and the claim wrote `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. This PR keeps the claim's line: it widens nothing (no single-walk verdict moves, no field is added) and narrows the `--json` `issues` shape.
